facts.detail: Ofcom published the tracker page on 27 February 2024.
The current tracker listing was updated on 14 May 2026.
Ofcom regularly monitors people's experience of communications services.
The tracker covers home-broadband affordability.
It covers mobile-phone affordability.
It covers landline affordability.
It covers pay-TV affordability.
The current listing presents an April 2026 multi-panel tracker series.
The page records low-base-size caveats for social-tariff awareness breakdowns.
Financial vulnerability combines income, work status and household size into three groups.

guard_streams.source: Latest trends in home broadband performance revealed
guard_streams.write_limit: Panel and provider measurements at routers are aggregate performance evidence and cannot be assigned as measured speed to a selected parcel.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the performance update on 17 March 2023.
The research uses volunteer router-monitoring units and provider data.
Average UK home-broadband download speed was 65.3 Mbit/s in September 2022.
The average was 10% higher than in March 2022.
Less than 3% of households averaged below 10 Mbit/s.
Ninety-three percent of researched homes used packages advertised at 30 Mbit/s or higher.
Ten percent used packages advertised at 300 Mbit/s or higher.
Average upload speed reached 15.5 Mbit/s, up 46% from March 2022.
Average 8pm-to-10pm download speed was 5% below average maximum speed.
A surveyed 1.1 Gbit/s cable package recorded the fastest average download speed.

guard_streams.source: Ofcom publishes framework to improve fairness for customers
guard_streams.write_limit: A fairness-assessment framework concerns provider conduct and cannot establish parcel-level broadband availability or speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the fairness framework on 23 January 2020.
The page was last updated on 17 March 2023.
The framework explains how Ofcom judges whether customers are treated fairly.
It followed a fairness commitment by the UK's biggest providers.
Ofcom considers whether customers receive clear information throughout the customer journey.
It considers whether making a complaint is straightforward.
It considers whether problems are fixed promptly.
Ofcom gives particular attention to harm affecting vulnerable customers.
The assessment considers harm significance, number of customers and duration.
It considers whether the service is important or essential to customers.

guard_streams.source: New Ofcom research reveals how to cut phone and internet bills
guard_streams.write_limit: Market-price, switching and usage statistics are aggregate consumer evidence, not selected-parcel broadband coverage or measured speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the research article on 26 February 2026.
The article was last updated on 30 June 2026.
Ofcom cites end-of-contract alerts, simpler summaries and easier switching.
Available broadband prices fell by 6% on average in real terms.
Twenty-eight percent of broadband customers were out of contract.
In-contract customers spent £7 to £9 less per month on average.
Eighteen percent of households switched internet provider, compared with 14% in 2023.
One Touch Switch had been used by more than two million customers.
Around eight in ten UK homes had access to full-fibre broadband.
Seventy percent of bundled landline households made no outgoing call and standalone broadband typically cost about £7 less.

guard_streams.source: Latest home broadband performance trends revealed
guard_streams.write_limit: Router and provider performance studies are aggregate measurements and cannot be written as selected-parcel measured speed.

facts.detail: Ofcom published the research update on 14 September 2023.
The research uses router measurements and data from the four largest broadband providers.
Average home-broadband download speed was 69.4 Mbit/s in March 2023.
Average download speed increased 17% year on year.
Eighty-eight percent of lines averaged at least 30 Mbit/s over 24 hours.
The comparable March 2022 proportion was 83%.
Three percent of connections averaged below 10 Mbit/s.
Average upload speed reached 18.4 Mbit/s, a 73% year-on-year increase.
The peak-time urban-rural average-speed gap was 26%, down from 58% in 2022.
Average cable speed was 270.6 Mbit/s and full-fibre average speed was 149.2 Mbit/s.
